title: SLA-aware priority queues and region-prefetch for relevance sorter
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Our relevance sorter (reranker) is the main tail-latency and throughput bottleneck for customers with mixed SLAs (interactive chat vs. bulk similarity jobs). We see P95/P99 spikes when bursty interactive traffic competes with large batched similarity requests across regions. Existing fallbacks reduce failures but cause user-visible quality regressions.

Goal: Implement an SLA-aware admission and priority queuing layer plus proactive regional prefetching and KV-cache warmup so the relevance sorter meets interactive SLOs (P95 < 120ms for small queries), maintains throughput for bulk workloads, and reduces cross-region failover frequency. Provide deterministic behaviors under overload and clear observability for routing and degradation decisions.

Approach:
- Introduce a two-tier priority queue (interactive vs bulk) in the frontend router with per-customer SLA tokens.
- Implement SLA-aware admission control that consumes tokens and applies backpressure or graceful degradation when tokens are exhausted.
- Add a lightweight circuit breaker per region/model-variant with configurable trip thresholds and automatic decay.
- Region-prefetch: when routing a request, prefetch KV/cache prefixes to the selected serving region when request mix indicates likely reuse (heuristics based on embedding namespace and recent hot keys).
- Fast local fallback: maintain a small LRU local embedding cache and a compact low-cost fallback reranker (smaller quantized model) to serve 99th percentile spikes with minimal quality loss.
- Metrics and checkpoints: tag every request with decision trace (queue priority, admission outcome, prefetch hit/miss, breaker state) for per-customer dashboards and SLO dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
1) For interactive class (<=64 tokens), median latency unchanged and P95 < 120ms in 99% of 24h windows under synthetic mixed workload (ratio 70:30 interactive:bulk).
2) Bulk throughput maintained within 15% of baseline when not contending with abnormally high interactive traffic.
3) Circuit breaker trips reduce error rate/service saturation events by >=40% during overload windows.
4) Prefetch hit-rate >30% for identified hot namespaces within first 30s of workload change.
5) Instrumentation surfaces clear traces in console per request and a new per-customer SLO alerting rule.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout in two phases: (1) priority queue + admission control + observability in canary region, (2) region-prefetch + local fallback + breakers enabled gradually with canary traffic and opt-in customers.
updates: 2026-02-15: Spike repro harness created in staging to simulate mixed interactive/bulk traffic (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/relevance-harness/pull/112).
2026-02-20: Benchmarked baseline: P95 interactive 210ms in mixed workload; bulk throughput 18k QPS steady (Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/rr-baseline).
2026-02-25: Design review with PM and Design completed; agreed on two-tier queue and token model; notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/SLA-aware-queue-design.
2026-03-01: Prototype of priority queue implemented behind feature flag in router-service; unit tests added; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router-service/pull/389.
2026-03-03: First canary run with 5% of traffic: observed P95 drop to 130ms for interactive but bulk throughput dropped 10%; traced root cause to aggressive token consumption for multi-turn sessions.
2026-03-05: Token model adjusted to account for session reuse; added token refill heuristics per-session; new canary shows P95 118ms and bulk throughput impact reduced to 6%.

2026-03-07: Implemented simple region-prefetch MVP (prefetch of top-10 KV prefixes per namespace) and a lightweight LRU embeddings cache (capacity 10k keys) in serving runtime; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/542.

2026-03-08: Load test with regional failover scenario: circuit breaker tripped in 2/3 simulated overloads and prevented cascade failures; we captured decision traces to tracing service (https://tracing.redwood/internal/trace/rr-50641).
